description: WHEN OTHER on the write - app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:267-273. All five fields arrive populated, so the EVALUATE TRUE at :117-151 falls through every blank arm to WHEN OTHER at :148-150, the guard IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON at :153 is therefore true, :154-158 build SEC-USER-DATA and WRITE-USER-SEC-FILE runs at :159. The forced outcome is NOT_FOUND, RESP 13 - a perfectly well-known CICS response that the EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :250-274 simply does not name - so it falls to the default arm rather than to the NORMAL arm at :251-259 or the shared DUPKEY/DUPREC arm at :260-266. Three details are pinned because each is easy to get wrong. The cursor is FNAMEL from :272, NOT the USERIDL the duplicate arm uses seven lines above it at :265. The arm emits no diagnostic: the DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD at :268 is commented out in this program, unlike the live equivalents in COUSR00C and COUSR03C, so expectedMessages carries the screen's two channels and no DISPLAY_LINE. And nothing is written: expectedWrites is empty, which asserts positively that no record was added, so the otherwise valid user id NEWUSR01 must not appear in USRSEC. Width derivation, summed mechanically from the PICTURE clauses rather than counted by eye: the literal 'Unable to Add User...' is 21 characters; the MOVE at :270-271 lands it in WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) declared at :38, giving 21 + 59 spaces; MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :188 then narrows it to ERRMSGO PIC X(78) declared at app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:164, giving 21 + 57 spaces and losing the last two bytes. Both channels are stated in full at their declared widths and neither is trimmed. The ten seeded rows are asserted byte-identical at the copybook's width, and expectedDatasets pins USRSEC on the FINAL_STATE channel at exactly ten rows of eighty bytes - which is how 'no eleventh row exists' becomes a first-class assertion instead of something left to emerge from the unaccounted-row scan, and how the dataset's declared width is pinned at all. No WRITES-channel expectation is declared, deliberately: a dataset reaches that channel only when a record was actually written, and this path writes none, so asserting it there would report correct behaviour as a difference. USRSEC has no fixture in app/data/ASCII - the nine that exist are for other datasets - so the ten rows are the in-stream IEBGENER data of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:L35-L44, five of type A and five of type U, stated at the 57 characters the JCL carries. app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy declares 80: SEC-USR-ID X(08) + SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) + SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) + SEC-USR-PWD X(08) + SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) + SEC-USR-FILLER X(23). The absent span is that trailing FILLER, and the 57-to-80 pad has exactly one owner: it is declared in normalisations and applied at seed time, never at comparison time, so a width disagreement in a failure is always a real difference and never a missing declaration. Every SEND performs POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :214-233 first, so TITLE01O and TITLE02O carry the 40-byte literals of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22 - the '  Credit Card Demo Application (CCDA)   ' alternative at :21 is commented out - with TRNNAMEO 'CU01' and PGMNAMEO 'COUSR01C' from :36-37. FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at :216 is pinned to one frozen instant, 2022-07-19T23:12:34, taken from the source's own version footer at :298 and shared by every case in this folder, so CURDATEO is 07/19/22 and CURTIMEO is 23:12:34 and nothing here depends on a wall clock. The code page is named explicitly as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default. COUSR01C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY - zero occurrences of either - so no '*' marker and no per-field DFHRED exists anywhere in this program; the single attribute item it ever assigns is ERRMSGC, and only in the NORMAL arm at :254, so this arm leaves it at the default colour. *COPY DFHATTR. at :57 is commented out, and DFHAID and DFHBMSCA at :55-56 are IBM-supplied and absent from this repository, so every attribute and AID name used here is reproduced from IBM CICS documentation in common.BmsAttributes and common.CicsAid and traces to no file in this checkout. EIBCALEN is 160, the exact width of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA at app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44, and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1, so :83 takes the re-entry path to RECEIVE-USRADD-SCREEN at :89 and WHEN DFHENTER at :91. All conversation state - the commarea, the attention identifier and the screen values - travels in the payload, and nothing whatsoever is held on the server. The transaction ends at the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID at :107-110, so the termination is RETURN_TRANSID and the response echoes the commarea unchanged. expectedReturnCode is 0, verified rather than assumed: this program contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' and never moves to RETURN-CODE. SEC-USR-PWD PIC X(08) stays plaintext, exactly as COSGN00C compares it, because hashing it would change observable behaviour and is out of scope; the value is the 2022-vintage demo password already carried as in-stream JCL data in this repository and it guards nothing. Preserved as inherited behaviour rather than corrected: this arm is a catch-all for responses the program never enumerates, and the program's validation is just as unenumerated - the EVALUATE TRUE tests each field only for SPACES OR LOW-VALUES and never tests that USRTYPEI is 'A' or 'U', even though app/bms/COUSR01.bms:146-150 renders the 17-byte prompt '(A=Admin, U=User)' beside the one-byte USRTYPE field defined at :141-145. That prompt documents a two-value vocabulary the program does not enforce, and no allowed-values check may be added on the strength of it. The five blank-field arms are pinned by case02 through case06, case06 being the USRTYPEI arm at :142-147; case07 pins that only the earliest blank speaks; and case08 and case09 pin the two halves of the duplicate arm that this default arm must stay textually and positionally distinct from. Provenance: every expected value here is statically derived by structured reading of app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:117-151, :153-160, :184-196, :214-233 and :238-274, cross-checked against app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY for the twelve xxxI widths including USRTYPEI PIC X(1) at :84 and ERRMSGO PIC X(78) at :164, app/bms/COUSR01.bms:141-154 for USRTYPE LENGTH=1 and ERRMSG LENGTH=78, app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for SEC-USR-TYPE PIC X(01) and the 23-byte SEC-USR-FILLER, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22 for the titles, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44 for the commarea, and the app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:L35-L44 seed rows. It was NOT captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment: AAP section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers, among them the absence of any z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, and the absence of Language Environment CEE* services. No user rules were provided for this project, so enterprise-standard best practice governs instead of a rule document.
